s: To which rock system does the Nellore mica schist belt belong?
x: The Dharwar system of the Chittoor–Nellore region holds the Nellore mica schist belt.

s: Which is regarded as the oldest land mass in Andhra Pradesh?
x: No option can be established: Sanganakallu is a Neolithic site in Ballari, Karnataka, not an AP land mass, and the item comes from APPSC Group-II 2019's 'oldest basin in AP', whose answer is the Kadapa Basin (not offered here).

s: Steatite (soapstone) of the Cuddapah system is mainly associated with which district?
x: Steatite occurs in the Cuddapah system of Kadapa.

s: In which basin of Andhra Pradesh are oil and natural gas found?
x: The KG basin, with marine sediments in Krishna, Eluru, Kakinada and Konaseema districts, holds AP's oil and natural gas.

s: A proposed underground coal-gasification project near Recherla and Chintalapudi is associated with which district?
x: The proposed project near Recherla and Chintalapudi is in Eluru district. It is intended to produce gas, hydrogen, ammonia and urea.

s: Which of the following is NOT part of the Krishna-Godavari basin?
x: Barmer-Sanchore is in Rajasthan; the other three are KG-basin areas.

s: JHBDPL is the pipeline of which project?
x: JHBDPL is the Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga pipeline under One Nation One Gas Grid.

s: For what is Tatipaka in Andhra Pradesh known?
x: Tatipaka has an ONGC mini-refinery.

s: Which of the following refinery pairs is correctly matched?
x: HPCL's Visakhapatnam refinery is AP's main refinery; Tatipaka is an ONGC mini-refinery in Konaseema.

s: Which company has operated the Ravva shallow offshore field of the KG basin since 1996?
x: Ravva was discovered by ONGC in 1987 and has been operated by Cairn since 1996.

s: Which of the following KG-basin pairs is correctly matched?
x: KG-D6 is Reliance's deepwater discovery; Ravva is operated by Cairn, Tatipaka is ONGC and Deen Dayal West was GSPC's.

s: Which company discovered the Ravva oil and gas field in the Krishna-Godavari basin in 1987?
x: ONGC discovered Ravva in 1987; Cairn has operated it since 1996.

s: Which company bought 80% stake and operatorship of GSPC's Deen Dayal West block in the KG basin in 2017?
x: ONGC took 80% and operatorship of the Deen Dayal West block (KG-OSN-2001/3) from GSPC in 2017.

s: To what share does India aim to raise natural gas in its energy mix by 2030?
x: India plans to raise the gas share from about 6.7% to 15% by 2030 under One Nation One Gas Grid.

s: Which river basins are important in northern Andhra Pradesh?
x: Vamsadhara and Nagavali are the northern basins; Godavari, Krishna and Pennar are the State's major basins.

s: Red sanders, scientifically known as Pterocarpus santalinus, is endemic to which group of hills?
x: Red sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) is endemic to the Seshachalam, Palakonda and Lankamalla hills of Rayalaseema.

s: What is the forest cover of Andhra Pradesh?
o: 30,084.96 sq km, constituting 23.59% of the State
40,084.96 sq km, constituting 23.95% of the State
20,084.96 sq km, constituting 13.59% of the State
30,804.96 sq km, constituting 32.59% of the State
x: Andhra Pradesh has 30,084.96 sq km of forest cover, which accounts for 23.59% of the State’s area.

s: Where is the Girijan Cooperative Corporation (GCC) of Andhra Pradesh headquartered?
x: GCC, headquartered at Visakhapatnam, buys minor forest produce from tribals at fair prices.

s: Which place is Andhra Pradesh's raw-salt hub?
x: Naupada (Srikakulam) is AP's raw-salt hub; Gujarat leads India with ~78% of salt.

s: What is the area of the continental shelf of Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's continental shelf is about 33,227 sq km.

s: Under Phase I, a new fishing harbour is being built at Juvvaladinne in which district?
x: Juvvaladinne (Nellore) and Uppada (East Godavari) are new Phase I harbours.

s: As per the December 2024 remeasurement, Andhra Pradesh's coastline of about 1,053 km ranks where among Indian States?
o: Third, after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu
x: The December 2024 remeasurement gives AP 1,053.07 km, third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu; on the older 974 km figure AP was second after Gujarat.

s: Which State is the leading producer of salt in India?
x: Gujarat gives about 78% of India's salt; AP gives only about 1% despite its long coast.

s: Why does Rayalaseema receive its peak rainfall during October-November rather than during the main south-west monsoon period?
o: It is directly exposed to the Arabian Sea branch of the monsoon.
It lies in the rain-shadow and benefits relatively more from the north-east monsoon.
It receives winter rainfall from western disturbances.
Its rainfall is controlled exclusively by local convection in April.
x: Rayalaseema lies in the rain-shadow of the south-west monsoon and receives its peak rainfall in October-November from the north-east monsoon.

s: Which of the following region–feature pairs of Andhra Pradesh is correctly matched?
o: Humid coastal region – Low rainfall, droughts and extreme heat
Deltaic region – Cool conditions and high local rainfall
Semi-arid Rayalaseema – Low rainfall, droughts and extreme heat
Hill region – Fertile land fed by rivers

s: Which of the following is identified as the lowest-rainfall region?
x: The Anantapur–Hagari valley gets the least rain in AP, under about 51 cm a year, as it lies in the rain shadow.

s: Which region of Andhra Pradesh receives 125–200 cm of rainfall?
x: The north coast and agency get 125–200 cm; Kadapa–Kurnool 75–100 cm and the Rayalaseema interior under 70 cm.

s: What is the main cause of droughts and famines in Rayalaseema?
x: Rayalaseema's droughts come from low and erratic rainfall; its low population density is a result of droughts, not their cause.

s: Between which latitudes does Andhra Pradesh lie?
x: AP has a tropical monsoon climate and lies approximately between 12°41'N and 19°07'N.

s: How many agro-climatic zones does Andhra Pradesh have?
x: AP has six agro-climatic zones, including the Scarce Rainfall Zone (Kurnool and Anantapuramu).

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the climatic extreme in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Sileru-Sabari valleys are identified as the wettest area. Rentachintala is the hottest, Lambasingi the coldest, and the Hagari valley the driest.

s: The Sileru and Sabari valleys receive approximately how much rainfall?
x: The Sileru and Sabari valleys are among the wettest parts of AP, getting about 140–152 cm of rain. Below 51 cm is the Hagari valley, and 75–100 cm is typical of the dry deciduous belt.

s: Which is the hottest place in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Rentachintala in Palnadu is the hottest place in AP; Lambasingi is the coldest.

s: Which districts form the Scarce Rainfall agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Kurnool and Anantapuramu form the Scarce Rainfall Zone among AP's six agro-climatic zones.

s: Which is the coldest place in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Lambasingi in Alluri Sitharama Raju district is the coldest place in AP; Rentachintala is the hottest.

s: What is the average annual rainfall of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Andhra Pradesh gets an average of about 966 mm of rain a year.

s: In which month does the coastal belt of Andhra Pradesh receive its peak rainfall?
x: The AP coast gets its peak rain in July (south-west monsoon), while Rayalaseema peaks in October-November.

s: Under Koeppen's classification, which code denotes the hot desert climate of western Rajasthan?
x: Western Rajasthan is BWhw (hot desert); BShw is the semi-arid steppe of rain-shadow belts.

s: Under Koeppen's classification, the Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu has which climate type?
x: The Coromandel coast is As, monsoon with dry summer; Amw is the west coast south of Goa.

s: Which of the following Koeppen code–area pairs is correctly matched?
x: Cwg (monsoon, dry winter) covers the Ganga plain; Amw is the west coast, E the high Himalaya and Dfc Arunachal Pradesh.

s: Under Koeppen's classification, which climate type is found in Arunachal Pradesh?
x: Dfc (cold humid winter with a short summer) is the Koeppen type of Arunachal Pradesh.

s: Under Koeppen's classification, which climate type covers the rain-shadow belts and parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat and Haryana?
x: BShw is the semi-arid steppe type of the rain-shadow belts and parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat and Haryana; BWhw is the hot desert of western Rajasthan.

s: Under Koeppen's classification, which climate type is found in the High Himalaya and Ladakh?
x: Koeppen's E type (polar/tundra) covers the High Himalaya and Ladakh.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Trewartha's classification of Indian climates?
o: It modified Koeppen's scheme, keeping its temperature-rainfall logic
Caw (Ganga plain) corresponds broadly to Koeppen's Cwg
It classified climates mainly by vegetation and altitude, rejecting temperature and rainfall
H (Himalaya) corresponds broadly to Koeppen's Dfc/E
x: Trewartha did not reject temperature and rainfall; he modified Koeppen with the same temperature-rainfall logic, simplified for India.

s: Under Trewartha's classification, what does 'Am' denote?
o: Tropical rainforest of the west coast and North-East
x: Am is tropical rainforest of the west coast and North-East; Aw is the Peninsula, BS/BW steppe and desert, Caw the Ganga plain.

s: Thornthwaite classified climates mainly using which combination?
x: Thornthwaite used precipitation effectiveness expressed through moisture conditions and thermal efficiency represented by potential evapotranspiration.

s: In Thornthwaite's moisture regions of India, which type is found in the rain-shadow interior Deccan?
x: The rain-shadow interior Deccan is semi-arid; western Rajasthan and Kutch are the arid end.

s: In Thornthwaite's moisture classification, which type is the driest?
x: Thornthwaite's moisture order runs perhumid (A), humid (B), sub-humid (C), semi-arid (D) and arid (E), so arid is the driest type.

s: Trewartha's 'Caw' climate of the Ganga plain corresponds to which Koeppen type?
x: Trewartha's Caw (humid subtropical, dry winter) equals Koeppen Cwg of the Ganga plain, not Aw.

s: In Thornthwaite's moisture regions of India, which area falls under the arid type?
x: The arid type covers western Rajasthan and Kutch; the interior Deccan is semi-arid and the Western Ghats and North-East are perhumid.

s: In Thornthwaite's classification, which parts of India have a perhumid climate?
x: The perhumid (A) type, the wettest in Thornthwaite's scheme, covers the Western Ghats-west coast and the North-East.

s: Under Koeppen's classification, which is the broad climate type of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Aw — tropical wet and dry climate
x: Andhra Pradesh is classified as Aw, the tropical wet and dry or savannah climate.

s: How many missions does the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) have?
x: The NAPCC has eight missions, from Solar to Strategic Knowledge; there is no nuclear mission.

s: When was the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) launched?
x: The NAPCC was launched on 30 June 2008.

s: What was India's climate adaptation spending in FY 2022 as a share of GDP?
x: Adaptation spending was 5.6% of GDP in FY 2022; SAPCCs moved from mitigation (2010–15) to district-level adaptation from 2020.

s: Which State was the first to prepare a State Action Plan on Climate Change (SAPCC)?
x: Odisha was the first State to have a SAPCC, prepared in 2010.

s: The AP State Action Plan on Climate Change 2025-30 targets how many EV charging stations?
x: AP SAPCC 2025-30 has 8 energy-sector adaptation measures, including 1 lakh EV charging stations.

s: According to the DST climate vulnerability report (2021), which is the most vulnerable State of India?
x: Jharkhand tops the DST 2021 list of eight highly vulnerable states; Odisha, Assam and Bihar are also on the list but lower.

s: Which of the following is NOT among the eight highly vulnerable states in the DST climate vulnerability report (2021)?
x: The eight are Jharkhand, Mizoram, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Assam, Bihar, Arunachal Pradesh and West Bengal; Andhra Pradesh is not one.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the eight missions of the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)?
x: The eight NAPCC missions include Solar, Water and Green India, but there is no nuclear mission.

s: From 2020 onward, the State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCCs) shifted their focus to which of the following?
x: SAPCCs moved from mitigation (2010-15) to district-level adaptation from 2020 on.

s: The below-normal 2026 monsoon forecast for most of Andhra Pradesh was attributed to which phenomenon?
x: The forecast of a below-normal 2026 monsoon for most of Andhra Pradesh cited El Nino as a contributing factor.

s: Which year was India's warmest since 1901, with 446 heatwave days?
x: 2024 was India's warmest year since 1901 and recorded 446 heatwave days.

s: According to the WMO, by about how much was 2025 above the pre-industrial level?
x: WMO placed 2025 at about 1.43 C above pre-industrial; 2015-2025 were the eleven warmest years.

s: What was IMD's temperature anomaly for India in 2024, its warmest year since 1901?

s:

s: Which statement best describes the present condition of the Godavari delta?
